stories.headline: Indian PM Modi visits Norway for first time in 43 years, holds bilateral talks and India-Nordic Summit
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Norway on May 18–19 for the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in Oslo, his first visit by an Indian prime minister to Norway in 43 years. He called on King Harald V and Queen Sonja and held bilateral talks with PM Støre covering trade, clean technology, the India-EFTA TEPA agreement, and potential expansion of GPFG investment in Indian capital markets.

stories.headline: Equinor Q1 2026 earnings beat expectations; AGM approves dividend and buyback; European gas supply talks launched
stories.summary: Equinor reported Q1 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.48, beating consensus by 46%, driven by 10% production growth in Norway amid elevated energy prices. The May 12 AGM approved a $0.39 Q4 2025 dividend and a $375M share buyback tranche. Equinor also initiated talks with European consumers including Germany, UK, and Netherlands on long-term commitments for costlier upstream projects, with a May 18 Oslo meeting scheduled.

stories.headline: Stoltenberg presents revised national budget; parliament battles, oil fund risk warnings, and Stad tunnel axed again
stories.summary: Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg presented the revised 2026 national budget on May 12, proposing to reduce oil fund spending by 4.9 billion NOK versus the approved budget and warned that a Middle East-driven market shock could cut the oil fund's value by one-third. Stoltenberg again removed Stad skipstunnel from the budget, was grilled on broken interest-rate promises, and faces challenging multi-party negotiations to secure a parliamentary majority.

stories.headline: FrP reaches near-20-year polling highs at 31%; Listhaug emerges as dominant PM candidate despite racism scandal
stories.summary: Multiple polls this week show the Progress Party (FrP) at approximately 31%, double the support of Høyre and the party's highest polling in 18 years. FrP leader Sylvi Listhaug is rated the most preferred PM candidate on the centre-right by a wide margin. Polls came after, and were apparently unaffected by, revelations that an FrP adviser made racist comments about Pakistanis at the party's national conference; Listhaug condemned the remarks and the adviser was dismissed.

stories.headline: Norway revokes NSM missile export license to Malaysia, triggering diplomatic row and legal threats
stories.summary: Norway's Foreign Ministry confirmed it has revoked export licenses for the Naval Strike Missile (NSM) system sold to Malaysia under a 2018 contract with Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace, citing tightened oversight of sensitive defense technology exports amid Europe's shifting security landscape. Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim condemned the decision as 'unilateral and unacceptable' in a phone call with PM Støre, and Malaysia's defense minister announced plans to claim compensation and consider legal action, with Malaysia having paid nearly 95% of the contract value.

stories.headline: Norges Bank surprises markets with 25bp rate hike to 4.25%; Norwegian krone strengthens
stories.summary: Norges Bank raised its key policy rate by 25 basis points to 4.25% on May 7, the first hike since 2023, citing persistent domestically-driven inflation. The move surprised markets and strengthened the Norwegian krone significantly versus the Swedish krona and other currencies. Major Norwegian banks including DNB and SpareBank 1 subsequently announced rate increases of up to 0.25 percentage points on mortgages and deposits.

articles.title: Central banks: Norgesbank takes market by surprise
